findings.msg: Scan quality acceptable. Book spread photos (two-page spreads from bound volume, fingers visible). Layout overlay shows correct region detection despite photographic distortion.
OCR text excellent despite book-spread scan source. Dense philosophical French prose reads coherently. Complex argumentation on development, rationality, and social institutions accurately captured.

Layout correctly handled. Page 1 starts with Raymond Aron's introduction, then Hersch's essay begins. Roman-numeral sections (I, II, III) correctly separated. Running headers and page numbers captured.
TEI VALID. 0 schema errors, 0 project errors, 0 warnings.
False positive entity: '<placeName ref="#zbz-l.13">Est</placeName>-ce' -- French verb 'Est' (is) at sentence start falsely tagged as place name (East). Occurs at least twice.
Entity type mismatch: 'Antigone' tagged as bibl (#zbz-w.838) -- in context refers to the character/person, not the play. 'Ismene' (#zbz-p.617) correctly tagged as person.
Entities: 78p 3o 5l 4w = 90. Density appropriate. Key persons (Raymond Aron, Jeanne Hersch, Ginsberg, Schaff, Simone Weil, Max Weber, Platon, Socrate, Oppenheimer) correctly tagged.

Document coherent: 'Developpement, conduites humaines et institutions sociales' -- philosophical essay responding to Ginsberg and Aron on development, rationality, and moralization. Begins with Aron's introduction, followed by Hersch's 3-part essay. Date unknown (metadata says 'unknown'). Ends with conclusion on freedom and rationality. Complete.
